At the federal level, the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act (MMA), the Social Security Act (SSA), and the Medicare Beneficiary Protection Act (MBPA) set the statutory framework for payment, quality measurement, and beneficiary protection. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) issues guidance through its Medicare Advantage Program Regulations (42 CFR Part 441) and supplemental policy documents that define payment methodology, audit procedures, and quality bonus structures. The clause must require the plan sponsor to provide timely access to data, maintain accurate electronic health record (EHR) documentation, and submit periodic audit reports in accordance with CMS’s “Audit Procedures for Medicare Advantage Plans” guidance. The agreement should also require the plan sponsor to implement corrective action plans within a specified timeframe and to notify the contracting entity of any CMS audit outcomes or proposed penalties.

**Quality‑Deficiency Liability Safeguards**  
The contract must embed a “Quality Assurance” clause that ties payment adjustments to performance on CMS‑approved quality metrics, such as those used in the Medicare Advantage Quality Bonus Program (MAQBP) and the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS). This provision should stipulate minimum score thresholds, define the calculation methodology for bonus or penalty payments, and require the plan sponsor to submit quarterly quality reports. An indemnification mechanism is essential: the plan sponsor shall indemnify the contracting entity against any financial loss resulting from CMS‑imposed quality penalties, provided that such penalties are attributable to documented deficiencies in care delivery or data reporting.
